rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Designates a `from` Vulnerability's details were tracked, aggregated, and/or enriched to improve context (i.e. NVD) by each `to` Agent.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: other
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Used when the type does not match any of the other options.
The product lifecycle phase, the requirement is applicable for.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: other
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relationship has other specific context information necessary to capture that the above set of enumerations does not handle.
A probability score between 0 and 1 of a vulnerability being exploited.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: partialAutomation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Level 2 - Partial automation or task automation. Some sub-functions of the system are fully automated while the system remain under control of an external agent. The system can perform actions for an approved task without requiring the agent's continuous direct control.
Identifies all the text and metadata associated with a license in the license XML format.
Specifies the type of an external reference.
These categories help define sets Responsibility Type.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: expandsTo
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element expands out as an artifact described by each `to` Element.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: regulation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A mandatory legal specification issued by a governmental or regulatory authority. Compliance is enforceable by law.
Provides an IntegrityMethod with which the integrity of an Element can be asserted.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: development
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relationship has specific context implications during development phase of an element.
A license addition that is not listed on the SPDX Exceptions List.
Quantity is the amount in the selected QUDT unit.
Records if sensitive personal information is used during model training or could be used during the inference.
Identifies the text of one or more copyright notices for a software Package, File or Snippet, if any.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: packagedBy
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Every `to` Element is a packaged instance of the `from` Element (`from` packagedBy `to`).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: attend
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The vulnerability requires attention from the organization's internal, supervisory-level individuals. Necessary actions include requesting assistance or information about the vulnerability, and may involve publishing a notification either internally and/or externally. CISA recommends remediating Attend vulnerabilities sooner than standard update timelines.
The location for picking up a package or item.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: analyzed
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: SBOM generated through analysis of artifacts (e.g., executables, packages, containers, and virtual machine images) after its build. Such analysis generally requires a variety of heuristics. In some contexts, this may also be referred to as a "3rd party" SBOM.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: observation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Documentation of direct monitoring or witnessing of the demonstration of processes, tests, or any kind of system responses during a specified timeframe under specified environmental conditions.
Provide consumers with comments by the creator of the Element about the Element.
A text describing the actual need defined by the requirement.
The result of applying a hash algorithm to an Element.
Maps a "LicenseRef-" string for a custom license or a "AdditionRef-" string for a custom license addition to a `CustomLicense`, a `CustomLicenseAddition`, or a `SimpleLicensingText`.
This is the agent that performed the act of destroying the item.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: finetunedOn
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element has been finetuned on the `to` Element(s).
Location of a specific action.
Provides information about the completeness of relationships.
Class that describes an InstantiateVirtualHardwareProcess that is used to define VirtualHardware and its source.
How the dataset was collected.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: inconclusive
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Inconclusive refers to a result or outcome from a verification, test, or analysis that cannot be clearly classified as either positive (successful, pass) or negative (failed, reject). An inconclusive result means there was not enough clear evidence, data, or signal to make a definitive determination, and further investigation or additional testing is necessary. An inconclusive result always shall need a comment on it.
A name used in a CdxPropertyEntry name-value pair.
The point in time when an element or an action starts, becomes applicable, or becomes valid.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: file
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The file represents a single file (default).
Portion of an AnyLicenseInfo representing a set of licensing information where all elements apply.
Text specifying a province or state.
Enumeration of dataset types.
Provides an ExternalMap of Element identifiers.
Regulation represents a rule or directive maintained by an authority.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: track
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The vulnerability does not require action at this time. The organization would continue to track the vulnerability and reassess it if new information becomes available. CISA recommends remediating Track vulnerabilities within standard update timelines.
Energy consumed when training the AI model that is being used in the AI system.
Provides the location of an exploit catalog.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: tracedToDetail
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: the `from` Requirement is refined and further elaborated by each `to` Requirement, which contains more detailed implementation information.
Hazards are potential sources of harm, danger, or adverse effects to people, property, the environment, or systems within or related to a specific piece of hardware.
The headquartersLocation defines the location of the organization's headquarters.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: phoneNumber
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Phone number; A string of decimal digits that uniquely indicates the network termination point defined in [RFC 3966](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc3966/) Section 5.
Identifier for product production batch.
Provides a set of values to be used to describe the common types of SBOMs that tools may create.
EvaluationResultType describes the outcome of an evaluation or verification process with.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: evaluatedOn
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element has been evaluated on the `to` Element(s).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: notAutomated
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Level 0 - Not automated. No automation. The operator fully controls the system.
Identifies the full text of a LicenseAddition, in SPDX templating format.
The planned location that a good, product or material is stored.
Identifies the full text of a License or Addition.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: runsOn
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element (the instructions) of runs on each `to` Hardware (processing element), during a LifecycleScopeType period.
Specifies whether the License is listed as approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
The amount or measure of a bulk product.
Provides the license under which the SPDX documentation of the Element can be used.
Sets the context for an assessment iby specifying the related project.
Specifies the exploit catalog type.
Street address includes a street number, name and unit ID to identify a specific street.
